answer: Cap seats per network origin. Each agent must answer a signed challenge from its own IPv4 /24 prefix, and each prefix holds one voting seat, with at most 50 seats per autonomous system. A clone farm hiding in one data-center oasis collapses into a single seat; to multiply it would need a whole atlas of separate provider routes. Proxy rings stand out as their addresses spiral through the same few prefixes. Leasing 500 distinct /24 blocks at about $300 a month each costs roughly $150,000 monthly.
